title: Exclude repeated two-stage scalar decoders through 32 power blocks
body:
Reusing the same two native stages does not give a short scalar decoder for the pinned center-free code. This is a **scoped negative result**: every nonempty reduced product with at most 32 alternating power blocks, and arbitrary nonzero integer exponents, still needs a scalar ADD count that grows with tensor width. **There is no cheaper circuit or new complete kappa bound.** The selected conditional kappa remains 0.0030217758.

The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2f5171c882dbc55815a63234e8bda1054921136f/research/repeated-native-code-separation/PROOF.md), [exact receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2f5171c882dbc55815a63234e8bda1054921136f/research/repeated-native-code-separation/RESULT.json) and [moment certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2f5171c882dbc55815a63234e8bda1054921136f/research/repeated-native-code-separation/MOMENTS.json) contain the result. The new finite witness proves independence for **every choice of coefficients**: the 64 nonconstant reduced projection words through degree 32 remain independent after removing the central-address output. Their 64-by-64 Gram determinant is exactly `52006 mod 65521`.

This witnesses a surviving native path which moves the central axis. A tensor-entry contraction then proves `ADDs >= max(0, 2f - 3r)`, where `r` is a finite product-dependent constant. No small value of `r` is claimed. The code identity `C_s^a = I + ((-13)^a - 1) P_s` extends the result to arbitrary nonzero integer powers and inverse products.

The scope has one shared binary axis, two private eight-axis blocks, and the exact [owner code](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/coded-native-caller/CODE.json) and [signed normalizers](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/coded-native-caller/NORMALIZERS.json). Adjacent inverse powers can cancel before reduction. The result does not cover longer reduced words, three or more stages, changed normalizers, paid Gaussian decoders, or callers with retained correlated inputs. It does not rule out another architecture.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 and NumPy 2.5.4:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/repeated-native-code-separation
```

Expected scientific marker:

```text
PASS_REPEATED_NATIVE_CODE_DEGREE32_NO_NEW_KAPPA
```

The registered dense replay and optimized certificate check pass. A separate C++17 replay, compiled with `-O3 -Wall -Wextra`, reproduces all **7,280 moment entries** through the eight-mode factorization; the dense replay uses the full owner matrix instead. Its binary64 operations are exact integer products and sums below `2^24`, with checked bounds. No floating-point rank test is used. Modular elimination and fraction-free integer elimination give the same determinant. Six boundary/rejection controls pass. Three optimized corruption runs reject changed phase bytes, a changed moment, and a forged receipt. Committed-byte, 16-file official export, export-integrity and Git-free optimized certificate checks pass. The [validation record](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2f5171c882dbc55815a63234e8bda1054921136f/research/repeated-native-code-separation/VALIDATION.md) and [README](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2f5171c882dbc55815a63234e8bda1054921136f/research/repeated-native-code-separation/README.md) give commands and limits. Hosted CI is separate and was not yet available when this description was prepared.

This is a certificate-assisted written proof with two replay implementations. Independent human or proof-kernel acceptance is not claimed. No full supplier/controller admission, compiler/outer replay, selected cold replay, Lean or Docker build was run. No full-history ancestry check was run in this shallow checkout.

Base: canonical main `1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4`, priority revision 7. Only the new scoped package changes. [Source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2f5171c882dbc55815a63234e8bda1054921136f/research/repeated-native-code-separation/SOURCES.json) bind all consumed bytes. The [canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4930#discussioncomment-19156644) distinguishes this work from the coupled-helper caller, paid-cache, geometry and border-grading tasks. A live prepublication check found no replacement for this exact repeated-code certificate. Sparse local-note coverage remains incomplete.

Credit Dillon's [PR #4933](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4933) for the physical code and normalizers; Dugongue's [PR #4929](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4929) for the center-free offer and spectrum; Cinna Davis's [PR #5065](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5065) for the two-stage terminal predecessor; and Ali Romman's [PR #5408](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5408) and its [pinned proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/256126eeb1607c0bf52996c3d90490f2b786b94a/research/fresh-stage-code-separation/PROOF.md) for fresh-stage separation and path contraction. The present change replaces fresh-stage uniqueness by a repeated-stage Gram witness. Cao Yifan, zxv, Jacob Alan Sussman and the cumulative lineage retain credit in the [source notice](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/coded-native-caller/NOTICE).
